title: IRS Publication 525 (2025), Foreign currency transactions
verified_text: If you have a gain on a personal foreign currency transaction because of changes in exchange rates, you don’t have to include that gain in your income unless it’s more than $200. If the gain is more than $200, report it as a capital gain.
limitation: IRS publication guidance; does not establish this taxpayer's facts.

title: 26 U.S.C. § 988 (2024 edition), Treatment of certain foreign currency transactions
verified_text: Covered foreign currency gain or loss is generally ordinary; disposition of nonfunctional currency is a section 988 transaction; personal transactions are excepted; personal currency gain is not recognized unless the gain on the transaction exceeds $200.
limitation: 2024 code edition; current applicability and taxpayer classification require professional confirmation.

title: IRS LB&I Concept Unit FCU/CU/C-18.2.1_04, Character of Exchange Gain or Loss on Currency Transactions
locator: General Overview; Disposition of Nonfunctional Currency
verified_text: Gain or loss from disposing of nonfunctional currency is determined by the change in exchange rates between acquisition and disposition; personal-transaction exception exists.
limitation: IRS training material dated 2016; not legal authority.

title: IRS Publication 551 (12/2025), Basis of Assets
verified_text: Basis is the amount of your investment in property for tax purposes; basis of property you buy is usually its cost; keep accurate records of items affecting basis.
limitation: General basis guidance; special acquisition rules may apply.

title: IRS Topic no. 409, Capital gains and losses
locator: Capital gains and losses; Short-term or long-term; Capital gains tax rates
verified_text: Capital gain or loss is amount realized minus adjusted basis; personal-use property losses are not deductible; holding period generally more than one year for long-term; page states 2025 capital-gain rate thresholds.
limitation: Rate thresholds on the retrieved page are labeled 2025; do not apply them to an unknown tax year without confirmation.

title: IRS Instructions for Schedule D (Form 1040) (2025)
locator: Basis and Recordkeeping; Short- or Long-Term Gain or Loss
verified_text: You need to know basis to figure gain or loss; keep accurate records; short-term holding period generally one year or less, long-term generally more than one year.
limitation: Form instructions; taxpayer-specific reporting position not determined.

title: IRS Instructions for Form 1116 (2025)
locator: Part III, Line 10; Line 12; categories and limitations
verified_text: You can carry back 1 year and then forward 10 years unused foreign taxes in a separate category that exceed the limitation, subject to restrictions; taxes on excluded income are reduced; no carryovers for section 951A category income.
limitation: Carryover rules are not a general 10-year refund window for all PRC taxes.

title: IRS Foreign Tax Credit
locator: Qualifying foreign taxes; How to claim; Compliance issues
verified_text: Credit may be available for foreign taxes imposed on you and subject to U.S. tax on the same income; generally only income, war profits and excess profits taxes qualify; no credit for taxes on excluded income; if entitled to treaty-reduced rate, only that reduced tax qualifies.
limitation: The page's general-looking 10-year refund paragraph is under French CSG/CRDS guidance, not a general PRC FTC rule.

title: IRS Yearly average currency exchange rates
locator: Translating foreign currency; Currency exchange rates; China row
verified_text: IRS has no official exchange rate; generally accepts any posted exchange rate used consistently; generally use spot rate when receiving, paying or accruing; China yuan 2025 yearly average is 7.129.
limitation: Yearly average is a reference, not necessarily the transaction-date spot rate.

title: IRS Report of Foreign Bank and Financial Accounts (FBAR)
locator: Who must file; When to file; Keeping records
verified_text: U.S. person must file if aggregate value of foreign financial accounts exceeded $10,000 at any time during the calendar year; due April 15 with automatic extension to October 15; records generally kept five years.
limitation: Penalty amounts are inflation-adjusted and fact-dependent; not estimated here.

title: IRS Do I need to file Form 8938?
locator: You must file Form 8938 if; thresholds
verified_text: Thresholds depend on specified person, specified foreign financial assets, residence abroad and filing status; U.S. unmarried $50,000 last day / $75,000 any time; abroad non-joint $200,000 / $300,000; joint thresholds higher.
limitation: Residence-abroad definition and asset aggregation require facts.

title: Treasury Reporting Rates of Exchange, as of September 30, 2026
limitation: Official reporting rate, not an executable bank conversion quote; PDF excludes online amendments.

title: Treasury Reporting Rates of Exchange dataset
verified_text: Quarterly official reporting rates; not current rates of exchange; amendments may appear online; exceptions include foreign currencies sold for dollars.
limitation: Do not use as a live CNY→USD transaction quote.

title: IRS Publication 54 (12/2025), Tax Guide for U.S. Citizens and Resident Aliens Abroad
verified_text: U.S. citizens and resident aliens are generally subject to U.S. income tax on worldwide income regardless of where they live; foreign tax credit may be available for foreign income taxes.
limitation: General guidance; filing requirements and elections depend on facts.

title: IRS Foreign currency and currency exchange rates
verified_text: Amounts on U.S. tax return must be expressed in U.S. dollars; functional currency generally U.S. dollar unless required to use foreign currency; use exchange rate prevailing when receiving, paying or accruing.
limitation: Does not supply this account's acquisition or disposition rates.
